title: The contrasting galaxies NGC 1316 and 1317
caption: The galaxies NGC 1316 and NGC 1317, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope
celestial: NGC 1316, NGC 1317 · constellation Fornax · about 60 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Two galaxies with very different histories share this picture from the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope at ESO's La Silla Observatory in Chile. The larger one is NGC 1316, and on the right is its smaller companion, NGC 1317.
NGC 1317 appears to have lived a quiet, peaceful life. NGC 1316, by contrast, carries the scars of earlier mergers with other galaxies.

Galaxies grow partly by absorbing their neighbours. When one galaxy swallows another, the collision can scramble the larger galaxy's shape and leave behind disturbed features that last for a long time afterward. Seen side by side, this pair shows two possible paths, a galaxy that has been left alone and one whose past has been shaped by repeated encounters. Both lie about 60 million light-years away, in the constellation Fornax.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (23.25 x 21.46 arcminutes) and distance (60 million light years), the frame spans roughly 406,000 × 375,000 light-years. Its light set out about 60 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This visible-light image was made with the Wide Field Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope, using blue, visual and red filters plus an H-alpha filter for glowing hydrogen. The source does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Long exposures gather far more light than the eye, which could never pick out the faint scars of past mergers directly.
